To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have computed the Bartholdi Zeta function for a large class of graph bundles and coverings.
the Bartholdi Zeta functions of a bundle and of a covering of a graph are related to the Zeta functions of the base and the fiber, respectively.

we derive some formulae for the computation of the Bartholdi functions of a graph and of a covering of a graph, and we obtain the Bartholdi function of Schreier graph, Cayley graphs, and the cartesian product graph.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the Bartholdi's zeta functions of the regular coverings of a graph, the Barthold's zeta functions for the graph bundles with regular fibers, and the Bartholdi’s zeta functions of some other graph products.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Bartholdi function is a very useful tool to study the structure of a graph and its covering.
the Bartholdi Zeta function of a covering of a graph G by a group G can be computed by a finite algorithm, which can be implemented by a computer.
the Bartholdi functions of graph bundles can be computed by the same formulae as those of regular coverings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Bartholdi function of any covering space of a graph is a polynomial in the Bartholdi functions of the graph and the fiber.
the Bartholdi spectrum and the Bartholdi eigenvalues of any graph bundle or of any covering of a graph are determined by those of its fiber and the base graph.
the Bartholdi functions of all the graphs mentioned above can be computed by the same formula.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Bartholdi function is a natural tool to study the regular covering and the graph bundle.
the Bartholdi spectrum of a graph can be computed from the Bartholdi spectra of a smaller graph, a regular graph, and a group.
the computation of the Bartholdi function of a graph bundle is reduced to that of a graph.
